Q: IBKR ib_insync problem with placing stop limit orders in pre/post markets A:

You're manually managing orderId, parentId, and transmit flags across separate ib.placeOrder() calls can easily cause Trader Workstation (TWS) to lose track of the order group, leaving the parent and child unlinked and stuck waiting for a manual "Transmit" action. Mixing custom order IDs with ib.client.getReqId() often desynchronizes the ID sequence from TWS.

Try to place a pre/post-market stop-limit bracket order, let ib_insync handle order ID assignment automatically and place the parent order first to establish the reference orderId:

  • Let ib_insync assign IDs: Remove manual calls to ib.client.getReqId() and let the library manage order IDs natively.

  • Place the parent first: Transmit the parent limit order with transmit=False so TWS holds it without sending it to the exchange yet.

  • Place the child second: Reference the parent's assigned orderId via limit_order.orderId and submit the stop-limit order with transmit=True to release the entire bracket group.

Give this a shot:

from ib_insync import IB, Stock, LimitOrder, StopLimitOrder

# Connect to Interactive Brokers TWS or IB Gateway
ib = IB()
ib.connect("127.0.0.1", 7497, clientId=1)

# Define the contract (e.g., ORCL)
contract = Stock("ORCL", "SMART", "USD")

# 1. Create and place the Parent Limit Order (outside RTH)
limit_order = LimitOrder(
    action="BUY",
    totalQuantity=10,
    lmtPrice=160.00,
    outsideRth=True,
    transmit=False  # Hold in TWS until child is transmitted
)

# Placing the parent first populates limit_order.orderId automatically
limit_trade = ib.placeOrder(contract, limit_order)

# 2. Create and place the Child Stop-Limit Order linked to the parent
stop_limit_order = StopLimitOrder(
    action="SELL",
    totalQuantity=10,
    stopPrice=146.00,
    lmtPrice=145.00,
    parentId=limit_order.orderId,  # Link to the parent's ID
    outsideRth=True,
    transmit=True   # Transmits the entire bracket group to TWS
)

stop_limit_trade = ib.placeOrder(contract, stop_limit_order)

print("Bracket orders placed successfully outside RTH.")

Q: Which git.exe should I reference? A:

The different version are each one for a different purpose.

  • \Program Files\Git\bin\git.exe
    This is the actual git binary which is added to your path if you run it form any script etc.

    This entry found here in the git source script for windows:
    https://github.com/git-for-windows/build-extra/blob/69c134c3c2c46bce1083d5bd4596d26543ca5f0f/portable/release.sh

  • \Program Files\Git\cmd\git.exe
    This is the git which is run when you add installed and choose to add git to your cmd (windows path)

    This entry can be found here in the source : <File Id="GitExe" Source="cmd\\git.exe" /> https://github.com/git-for-windows/build-extra/blob/69c134c3c2c46bce1083d5bd4596d26543ca5f0f/msi/release.sh

  • \Program Files\Git\mingw64\bin\git.exe
    This is the git-bash version which is used by the git-bash cygwin emulator

    It defined here in the wxs (installer file)
    https://github.com/git-for-windows/build-extra/blob/69c134c3c2c46bce1083d5bd4596d26543ca5f0f/msi/GitProduct.wxs

      <?if $(var.SixtyFourBit)=64 ?>
      <Directory Id='MingwFolder' Name='mingw64' />
  <?else?>

  • \Program Files\Git\mingw64\libexec\git-core\git.exe
    This one is also for the emulator and is being defined here:
    https://github.com/git-for-windows/build-extra/blob/69c134c3c2c46bce1083d5bd4596d26543ca5f0f/git-extra/git-prompt.sh

    then
   GIT_EXEC_PATH="$(git --exec-path 2>/dev/null)"
   COMPLETION_PATH="${GIT_EXEC_PATH%/libexec/git-core}"
   ...

Q: how to unindent in vim without leaving edit mode? A:

In normal mode, == would trigger auto-indent for the current line, which is likely to set the desired indentation level.

Q: Prefix of string up to first numeric value A:

Please try the following solution based on the PATINDEX() function.

Returns the starting position of the first occurrence of a pattern in a specified expression, or zero if the pattern isn't found, on all valid text and character data types. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/sql/t-sql/functions/patindex-transact-sql?view=sql-server-ver17

Notable points:

  • PATINDEX() find the first occurrence of any numeric value [0-9].
  • LEFT() and SUBSTRING() functions are used to split college course into two pieces, i.e. course prefix and course code.
  • IIF() applies some protective logic to take care of outliers that were added to the data sample (id=3,4) where calculated pos=0.

SQL Server 2025 might simplify the solution by using newly introduced RegEx functions.

SQL

DECLARE @tbl TABLE (id INT IDENTITY PRIMARY KEY, course VARCHAR(30));
INSERT @tbl (course) VALUES
('Math10031C'),
('History10018D'),
('Physics'),
('10018T');

SELECT * 
    , LEFT(t.course, IIF(pos=0,LEN(t.course) + 1, pos) - 1) AS course_prefix
    , IIF(pos=0, '',  SUBSTRING(t.course, pos, LEN(t.course))) AS course_code
FROM @tbl AS t
CROSS APPLY (SELECT PATINDEX('%[0-9]%', t.course)) AS t1(pos);

Output

id course pos course_prefix course_code
1 Math10031C 5 Math 10031C
2 History10018D 8 History 10018D
3 Physics 0 Physics
4 10018T 1 10018T

Q: When clicking on a plotOutput produced by grid.draw in a Shiny app, how do I map the click's returned normalized parent coordinates to the data space? A:

When you render a ggplot via grid.draw() in Shiny, click coordinates lose their data-space mapping. Keep your plots as ggplot objects and render them with renderPlot() and you don't need no manual remapping. Panel alignment then comes from controlling the fixed-width elements around each plot rather than from grob surgery.

library(shiny)
library(ggplot2)

base_theme <- theme_gray() +
  theme(
    plot.margin  = margin(5, 10, 5, 5),
    axis.title.y = element_text(margin = margin(r = 8)),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(hjust = 1)
  )

df <- data.frame(
  plot = rep(1:4, each = 3),
  x    = c(1, 2, 3,  10, 20, 30,  0.1, 0.2, 0.3,  100, 200, 300),
  y    = c(4, 5, 6,  100, 200, 300,  1000, 2000, 3000,  0.01, 0.02, 0.03)
)

plots <- Map(function(d, i) {
  ggplot(d, aes(x, y)) +
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    labs(title = paste("Plot", i), x = "X", y = "Y") +
    base_theme
}, split(df, df$plot), 1:4)

ui <- fluidPage(
  fluidRow(
    column(6, plotOutput("plot1", click = "click1", height = "300px")),
    column(6, plotOutput("plot2", click = "click2", height = "300px"))
  ),
  fluidRow(
    column(6, plotOutput("plot3", click = "click3", height = "300px")),
    column(6, plotOutput("plot4", click = "click4", height = "300px"))
  ),
  fluidRow(column(12, verbatimTextOutput("clickInfo")))
)

server <- function(input, output, session) {
  
  output$plot1 <- renderPlot(plots[[1]])
  output$plot2 <- renderPlot(plots[[2]])
  output$plot3 <- renderPlot(plots[[3]])
  output$plot4 <- renderPlot(plots[[4]])
  
  fmt <- function(click, i) {
    if (is.null(click)) return(paste0("Plot ", i, ": no click yet"))
    paste0("Plot ", i, ": x = ", signif(click$x, 4),
           " , y = ", signif(click$y, 4))
  }
  
  output$clickInfo <- renderText({
    paste(fmt(input$click1, 1),
          fmt(input$click2, 2),
          fmt(input$click3, 3),
          fmt(input$click4, 4),
          sep = "\n")})
}

shinyApp(ui, server)

If all you're interested in is getting the coordinates for each panel, then this works. But if you have other requirements, please clarify.
